tips.title: Achieving a Smooth, Even Airbrush Finish with Minimal Overspray
tips.text: Use a high-volume, low-pressure (HVLP) airbrush with a 1.5-2mm nozzle and a 0.5-1.5mm air cap. Set the air pressure to 10-15psi and the paint flow to 5-10%. Use a medium to thin paint viscosity, and thin with a specialized airbrush thinner (e.g., Vallejo Airbrush Thinner) to achieve the desired consistency.

tips.title: Hand Painting Techniques for Realistic Edge Highlighting
tips.text: Use a fine-tip brush (0.1-0.3mm) and a mixture of 90% paint and 10% medium (e.g., Vallejo Medium Varnish) to create a blendable, soft edge highlight. Apply the highlight to the raised edges of raised details, such as rivets, bolts, or panel lines, using a gentle, sweeping motion.

tips.title: Choosing the Right Primer for Scale Model Painting
tips.text: Select a primer that matches the model's material and intended use (e.g., acrylic, enamel, or metallic). For example, use a flexible primer (e.g., Tamiya Flexible Cement) for models with flexible parts or a primer with a high filler content (e.g., AK Interactive Primer) for models with rough surfaces.

tips.title: Decal Application Techniques for a Smooth, Bubble-Free Finish
tips.text: Use a decal solution (e.g., Microscale Decal Settling Solution) to soften the decals and facilitate even application. Apply a thin layer of decal solution to the decal and let it sit for 1-2 minutes before applying it to the model. Use a gentle, smoothing motion to remove air bubbles and excess solution.

tips.title: Creating Realistic Weathering Effects with Washes and Dry Brushing
tips.text: Use a weathering wash (e.g., AK Interactive Wash) to create a subtle, realistic weathering effect on raised details, such as rivets, bolts, or panel lines. Apply the wash using a fine-tip brush (0.1-0.3mm) and a gentle, sweeping motion. For dry brushing, use a stiff-bristled brush and a light touch to create texture and wear on flat surfaces, such as hulls or wings.
